subject: ventures/roofing-insurance-supplement-finder
professional: a storm-restoration roofing contractor's insurance supplement specialist (or a licensed public adjuster) who writes Xactimate supplements daily; first checks: are waste, tear-off and install quantities handled the way Xactimate line items carry them (removal on net area, waste on the install line only), are code items (IRC 2021 R905.2.8.5 drip edge, R905.1.2 ice barrier) derived from eave and rake lengths, are steep and high charges tiered, is O&P added not compounded, and does the ACV / recoverable-depreciation arithmetic match how carriers pay

evidence.correctness: Ran calc.mjs on DEFAULTS and on a hip-roof case and recomputed every figure independently in Python from the README's own formulas and standard insurance arithmetic (ACV = RCV x (1 - depreciation) - deductible; recoverable depreciation paid on completion). Default example: shingle gap 3 sq x 465 + 31.5 x 70 = 3,600; missing lines 546 + 884 + 142.5 + 304 + 170 + 1,440 + 275 = 3,761.50; subtotal 7,361.50; O&P 20% = 1,472.30; tax 7,361.50 x 0.40 x 0.06 = 176.68; supplement RCV 9,010.48; depreciation 12/25 = 48%; ACV now before 4,884, after 8,163.82; on completion 18,007.34; grid cell 75%/15% = 5,744.18. All match to the cent. Hip roof 24.6 sq net at 15% waste vs 26 sq on estimate: 28.29 needed, 2.29 short, 961.80 at 420/sq: matches. Arithmetic is right on its stated model; the model's treatment of tear-off on waste squares and its quantity/price split are domain issues (see domain and defects), so 3 not 4.
evidence.completeness: README and page claims checked end to end: shingle quantity and price gap (works), eleven checked lines with missing/over split (works; README count of eleven matches LINES), O&P switch added not compounded (works), tax on material share (works), straight-line capped depreciation and deductible (works), recoverable switch (works), acceptance share (works), 4x4 acceptance-by-fee grid (works), usage opt-out and local-only counters (present, usage.test.mjs). page.test.mjs runs the page script against a DOM stub and prints the $9,010 headline. No stubs or TODOs; sibling links resolve; served llms.txt clean.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the subject: 31 tests, 31 pass, 85 ms. The calc tests use hand-checkable round inputs and pin the default worked example. Four seeded mutations with quality_mutate.py: removing the depreciation cap (caught), removing the 100% cap on percentages (caught), putting O&P into the tax base (caught), and treating a line measured 0 but on the estimate as 'unused' instead of 'over' (survived: the page filters 'over' rows for the 'more generous' table, so that line would vanish).
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (176 lines), index.html script, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs. Pure functions, no dependencies, NaN-safe via nz(). Defects: shingleGap names the at-your-price figure `quantityGap` while a local `quantityGap` is at their price (calc.mjs:86-98), a garbled comment 'Yearly-free grid' (calc.mjs:173), booleans entered as numeric 1/0 fields (index.html:94), and opts() silently replaces a blank or unparseable field with the example value (index.html:153), although it writes the value back so it is visible.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer (No warranty, not insurance/legal/public-adjuster advice), 'Not decided' section and privacy line present on the page and tested in page.test.mjs. Served llms.txt (node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs) links the marisstella.app page, no retired origin. 'Nothing leaves your browser' backed: page test forbids fetch/XHR/sendBeacon and remote scripts. 'Defaults are placeholders' stated. Weak claims: the page says to 'argue these separately: one is a measurement, the other a price' but the measurement figure it prints is priced at the contractor's price, so it carries part of the price argument; README says it lets you 'tell whether a supplement service's fee is worth paying', but it only shows net after a fee, with no comparison to the contractor's own time or the service's acceptance rate.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job a supplement specialist does: from an EagleView/Hover report (eaves, rakes, ridges, hips, valleys, pitch areas) and the carrier's Xactimate estimate, list missing and short line items and price them. The tool needs every quantity pre-derived by hand: starter, drip edge and ice barrier squares are not computed from eave and rake lengths; there are no Xactimate line codes, no supplement-letter or line-item export, steep charges are one tier for install only, and over-included lines cannot be netted into a defensible net request. Useful as a quick 'how much is on the table' check, not to finish a supplement. verticals.json marks it a front door for bet #6 (residential takeoff, bets.md rank 6, 'feeds the contractor suite later'), but the page has no link or call to action toward any paid product.
evidence.domain: Compared with Xactimate line-item practice and IRC 2021 R905. Departures: (1) one blended 'tear-off plus install' price per square is applied to squares that include waste, so the missing waste squares and the price gap carry tear-off labour on area that does not exist; in Xactimate removal is quantified on the net roof surface and waste is added only to the shingle install line. (2) Steep-slope charges in Xactimate are tiered (7-9/12, 10-12/12, over 12/12) and apply to both removal and install; here one line, one rate. (3) Code-required items (R905.2.8.5 drip edge at eaves and rakes, R905.1.2 ice barrier from the eave to 24 in. inside the exterior wall line where required) are typed quantities, not derived or flagged as code items. (4) The quantity/price split prices missing squares at the contractor's price, mixing the two arguments it says to keep apart. Right: O&P 10+10 added not compounded, tax on materials only, ACV less deductible with recoverable depreciation on completion, drip edge labelled eaves and rakes, 1 square = 100 sq ft.

defects.what: One blended 'tear-off plus install' price per square is applied to squares that include waste, so missing waste squares and the per-square price gap carry tear-off labour on roof area that does not exist; Xactimate quantifies removal on the net surface and adds waste only to the install line. The request is overstated by tear-off rate x missing waste squares (and x waste share of the price gap).

The page tells the user to argue the measurement and price gaps separately, but prices the missing squares at the contractor's price (1,395 on the default) and the price gap only on the estimate's squares (2,205); the measurement argument at the estimate's own price is 1,185 and the price argument on all needed squares 2,415. Same 3,600 total, wrong split for the two arguments.

Starter, drip edge and ice barrier quantities are typed, not derived from eave and rake lengths, and are not flagged as code items (IRC 2021 R905.2.8.5, R905.1.2); steep charge is one tier for install only, not Xactimate's three tiers for removal and install; no line codes or supplement export. A specialist still does the takeoff by hand.

A line measured 0 but present on the estimate is marked 'unused' only if both are 0, and a seeded change to that status rule survived every test; the 'more generous' table would silently drop such a line.
Front door to the residential-takeoff bet (verticals.json) but the page has no link or call to action toward any paid product.
README claims the tool tells 'whether a supplement service's fee is worth paying'; it only shows net after a fee, with no in-house cost or acceptance-rate comparison.

A blank or unparseable field is silently replaced by the example default (e.g. a cleared deductible becomes 2,500); booleans are numeric 1/0 fields; confusing quantityGap naming and a garbled 'Yearly-free grid' comment.

verdict: A small, clean, honest calculator whose arithmetic is right: the default supplement (9,010.48), the ACV and completion payments (8,163.82 / 18,007.34) and a hip-roof shingle gap recompute to the cent, 31 tests pass and three of four seeded mutants die. It meets the bar narrowly (correctness, claims and verification 3, median 3) but a supplement specialist would not sign off on its method: tear-off is priced on waste squares, the 'argue separately' split prices the measurement gap at the contractor's price, and code items, steep tiers and line codes are left to the user. Fitness 2: it sizes the money on the table but does not produce a supplement, and as a front door to the residential-takeoff bet it links to no paid product.
